name: Sky Blue (Crayola)
lede: Sky Blue (Crayola) is a bright, slightly green-leaning cyan that Crayola names as a variant of the plainer Sky Blue, rare enough in our painting archive that only a handful of matches turn up.

sections.title: A Crayola variant
sections.body:
Our library files this cyan as a Crayola crayon name, drawn from the core color [[sky-blue]] as a qualified variant rather than a separate word [1]. The books we checked carry no entry for it, and no ISCC-NBS or Ridgway filing exists in our library for this exact name, so its naming is undocumented beyond the Crayola box itself [1]. By our own nearest-match calculation it sits close to the ISCC-NBS category 'very light greenish blue,' though that is our computed match, not a 1955 dictionary filing [1].

The real look-alike nearest is [[calamine-blue]], duller than this cyan, with [[sky-blue]] itself bluer and a little further off, and [[robin-s-egg]] lighter and more vivid still; [[aqua-blue]] sits a little further out again, more vivid and bluer [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this cyan in 6 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, rarer than 82 percent of the named colors we track [3]. Inside those few paintings it plays a mid tone every time [3]. The earliest match is Juan de Barroeta's 1854 painting, with the latest from 1912, four dated paintings in all — too thin a sample, and a floor, not a first, given how little of the archive's early centuries survive [3].
